item.title: Woman faces holding charges after wielding cleaver at police in Sheung Shui
item.description: Three holding charges have been laid against a woman who was arrested on Saturday after she allegedly wielded a cleaver at police officers in a restaurant in Sheung Shui. Hong Kong police said on Wednesday that the woman, 32, was charged with one count each of possession of an offensive weapon, criminal damage, and assaulting […]

item.title: Hong Kong axes on-site same-day tickets for test-free driving licences after complaints about ‘queuing gangs’
item.description: The Hong Kong government has ended the distribution of on-site same-day tickets for people applying for Hong Kong driving licences without tests, following complaints about “queueing gangs.” Starting Thursday, on-site tickets for test-free Hong Kong driving licence applications are no longer available, the Transport Department said on Wednesday. item.title: Hong Kong cop charged with drink-driving, 3 other offences after crashing into police vehicle
item.description: A Hong Kong police officer has been charged with drink-driving and three other offences after crashing his car into a police vehicle. The off-duty officer was arrested late Tuesday night after his car hit a police vehicle on Concorde Road in Ngau Tau Kok, the force said. He subsequently failed a breathalyser test conducted by […]

item.title: Accused scam boss Chen Zhi arrested in Cambodia, extradited to China, Phnom Penh says
item.description: Chinese-born tycoon Chen Zhi, who was indicted by the United States on fraud and money-laundering charges for running a multibillion-dollar cyberscam network from Cambodia, has been arrested there and extradited to China, Phnom Penh said Wednesday. Chen allegedly directed operations of forced labour compounds across Cambodia, where trafficked workers were held in prison-like facilities surrounded […]

item.title: Veteran lawmaker Starry Lee elected as president of Hong Kong legislature
item.description: Veteran pro-Beijing lawmaker Starry Lee has been elected as the president of the Legislative Council (LegCo), defeating finance sector lawmaker Ronick Chan. Of the 90 sitting lawmakers, 89 cast their votes behind closed doors on Thursday, with one legislator absent and not casting a ballot. In the tightly run race, Lee won 47 votes, while […]

item.title: Hong Kong independent bookseller pleads not guilty to charges over running ‘unregistered school’
item.description: Hong Kong independent bookseller Pong Yat-ming has pleaded not guilty to five charges alleging that he ran an “unregistered school” at his Book Punch bookstore. item.title: Hong Kong man remanded into custody pending case over ‘seditious’ Facebook posts
item.description: A Hong Kong man has been charged under the city’s homegrown security law for repeatedly sharing Facebook posts that were deemed seditious. Chong Wai-man, 61, was brought to the West Kowloon Magistrates’ Courts on Thursday afternoon to face one count of “knowingly publishing publications that had a seditious intention.” He was remanded into custody pending […]

item.title: Japan nuclear regulator official loses phone with confidential data in China
item.description: An employee of Japan’s nuclear regulator lost a smartphone, possibly in China, containing a confidential list of contacts, an official and local media reports said. item.title: Bus passengers face HK$5,000 fine, 3-month jail for not wearing seat belts from Jan 25
item.description: Hong Kong will tighten its road safety regulations on January 25, with passengers who fail to wear seat belts on public transport and commercial vehicles facing fines of up to HK$5,000 and three months in prison. item.title: Hong Kong public hospital A&E visits drop following doubling of fees for low-priority cases
item.description: The number of patients visiting the Accident and Emergency Departments (A&E) at Hong Kong’s public hospitals has dropped after authorities more than doubled the fees from HK$180 to HK$400 for low-priority cases in a bid to curb misuse.
